what: Fair Isaac invents the FICO score, the credit score American lenders use to decide who gets a mortgage, a car loan or a credit card. It also sells software that banks use to decide and manage those loans.
customers: Banks, credit card issuers, mortgage lenders and the three credit bureaus, who pay per score pulled.
money: about half, and almost all the profit
royalties each time a FICO score is pulled for a lending decision
decision management, fraud detection and originations platforms
moat: A standard written into regulation and contracts. Mortgages sold to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac must carry a FICO score, so lenders cannot switch even when a rival score exists.
risks: The regulator that oversees Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac is pushing to allow a competing score on mortgages
$5.3B of debt against $218M of cash, the result of years of buying back stock
Mortgage volumes set how many scores are pulled, and they fall when rates rise
opportunities: A 32.9% net margin and $1.1B of free cash flow on $2.5B of revenue: among the highest margins of any listed company
Revenue grew from $1.4B to $2.5B in four years, mostly by raising the price per score
Analysts see about 21% upside, with 19 covering the stock
watch: Whether a competing mortgage score is actually adopted, and the price per score.
